title: Word2Vec: Skip-gram & CBOW
interviewAnswer: Word2Vec learns dense word embeddings from context prediction. Skip-gram predicts context from a center word; CBOW predicts center from context, producing representations with useful distributional similarity.
keyPoints: Static word has one vector regardless of context.
Negative sampling approximates expensive softmax training.
why: Word2Vec: Skip-gram & CBOW appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Static word has one vector regardless of context.
deepDive: Word2Vec learns dense word embeddings from context prediction. Skip-gram predicts context from a center word; CBOW predicts center from context, producing representations with useful distributional similarity. Negative sampling approximates expensive softmax training. Context window shapes semantics. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: “bank” has one vector even though river bank and financial bank differ, motivating contextual embeddings.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
